paper.title: LASER: LLM Agent with State-Space Exploration for Web Navigation
paper.central_claim: Modelling interactive web navigation as transitions among a small set of hand-defined states, each with state-specific instructions and permissible actions, lets an LLM agent backtrack from mistakes and always act validly; without in-context examples LASER significantly outperforms previous methods on WebShop and closes the gap with human performance on amazon.com, and transfers to other LLMs.
paper.scope_as_measured: WebShop 500 test instructions (GPT-4-0613, single run), ablations on 200, 100 amazon.com instructions converted to WebShop format and human-annotated by the authors.

assessment.author_claim_preserved: significantly outperforms previous methods and closes the gap with human performance on web navigation
assessment.strongest_supported_claim: In the interactive WebShop simulator with executable reward, a GPT-4-0613 agent with hand-written state-specific instructions and per-state actions reaches 50.0 SR vs 34.0 for a same-backbone ReAct rerun (48.4 without backup). The amazon.com arm is author-annotated and format-converted and does not meet the transfer bar; which component (states, action restriction, backtracking) causes the gain is not isolated.

G.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Concrete invalid-action and forward-only failures with observed ReAct behaviour (O12) and named nearest neighbour; prevalence not quantified.

M.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Per-state admissible actions directly remove invalid actions; recovery via back transitions plausible but not given a distinguishing measurable prediction.

X.reason: Both 3; confirmed. Full state prompts, action table, budget and backup rule disclosed (O06); temperature unstated and state enumeration manual (O11).

E.measurement.reason: Decided for son55. WebShop executable reward is credible for C1 (O01), but the human-parity claim rests on authors’ own manual attribute annotation on format-converted amazon pages (O02, O03) with no agreement estimate and a human baseline from another study; authors also report 9/30 sampled errors were arguably correct items (O08), i.e. checker strictness affects comparisons with human numbers.

E.causality.reason: Decided for sol. A same-backbone ReAct rerun (O04) and LASER without backup (O05) give a controlled comparison of the whole treatment (48.4 vs 34.0 on 500); son55’s "changes the backbone" applies to copied baselines, not to the rerun. Still no ablation removing the state formulation/restriction/backtracking with the same instructions, and the rerun underperforms its original (O12).

E.holdout.reason: Both 2; confirmed. Test set used once; amazon.com unused in development but same converted format and product family; single domain (O10).

E.statistics.reason: Both 1; confirmed. Single runs, ablations on 200 (O07) with 1.6–2 point differences interpreted, no intervals; 30-case Dev error audit.

E.cost.reason: Decided for sol. The material does report budget information relevant to this item — a 15-transition cap with forced selection at 13 (O06) and a trajectory-length distribution — so not_reported (0) is not correct; but no tokens, calls, latency or $ for LASER or baselines, and baseline step budgets unstated.

resolutions.reason: EVIDENCE.md requires online success (execution-checked) in an environment unused during construction. The amazon.com arm is judged by the authors’ manual attribute annotation (O03) with no agreement check, on pages converted into the development environment’s exact format (O02), stopping before purchase (O09). WebShop itself is interactive with executable reward → online. Transfer is therefore not established; amazon numbers retained as author-reported, unvalidated evidence.
State-specific instructions belong to the same structural operation; generic prompting is not a distinct operation; son55 rated it weak.
rs:C13 centres on message passing over a relational topology with a structural guarantee; LASER only constrains admissible actions. son55 rated the fit weak_partial.
Human-parity headline rests on unvalidated author annotation and a cross-study human baseline (O02, O03); WebShop checker credible but strict (O08).
Same-backbone ReAct rerun and −backup comparison (O04, O05) are relevant controlled results; component isolation missing → anchor 2, not 1.
Step cap and length distribution are reported budget evidence (O06), so the not_reported condition ("no applicable evidence after full search") does not hold; tokens/calls/$ absent → 1.
The web-navigation planning claim falls inside applies_when; WebArena predates and is cited.
Observation setting disclosed; no screenshot claim.
